findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is not datetime-aware but is used with order_by="-datetime"
findings.body: The audit-log endpoint instantiates `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, but this class copies the integer `Paginator` behavior: `get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the model attribute. For `AuditLogEntry.datetime` that attribute is a `datetime`, so on the first page with any results `build_cursor` calls `get_item_key` and raises `TypeError`, making `optimized_pagination=true` requests fail with a 500. Additionally, `value_from_cursor` returns the raw integer cursor value instead of converting it back to a datetime like `DateTimePaginator` does, so subsequent page queries would compare the timestamp column to an integer and fail or return incorrect results. The paginator needs `DateTimePaginator` semantics (multiplier and cursor conversion) or the endpoint must not use it.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch uses unsupported Django negative slicing
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is true and the cursor offset is negative, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` passes a negative start index into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets explicitly reject negative indexing/slicing with `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`, so any caller who supplies a cursor with a negative offset (possible through `Cursor.from_string`) receives a 500 instead of a page. The comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing is incorrect; the branch cannot work as written and should validate/reject negative offsets or use a supported pagination mechanism.

findings.title: Partial negative-offset clamping produces inconsistent pagination metadata
findings.body: The change clamps negative offsets to zero only when `cursor.is_prev` is false, but the original negative `offset` is still passed to `build_cursor`. For `is_prev=False`, a malformed cursor with a negative offset now returns the first page while `_build_prev_values` sees a truthy `offset` and emits a `prev` cursor with `has_results=True`, incorrectly telling the client there is a previous page. For `is_prev=True`, the offset is left negative and still hits Django's negative-slicing `ValueError`. Negative offsets should be validated consistently rather than partially clamped.

findings.title: No tests cover the new paginator, datetime usage, or negative cursors
findings.body: This PR adds a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and an endpoint branch that uses it, but adds no tests. A basic non-empty audit-log request with `optimized_pagination=true` would have exposed the datetime `TypeError`, and a cursor with a negative offset would have exposed the invalid negative slice. Tests should cover the datetime endpoint path, cursor round-tripping, and negative/malformed cursor handling.
